source_refs.note: Exercise 14.3, Question 12: (u + v) x (u - v) = -2(u x v) (book p.283). Proof, no key answer.

blocks.prompt: 12. Use the definition of cross product, prove that for any vectors \(\underline{u}\) and \(\underline{v}\): \((\underline{u} + \underline{v}) \times (\underline{u} - \underline{v}) = -2(\underline{u} \times \underline{v})\)
blocks.explanation:
Definition se nikle hue qawaneen (properties) se proof.
Do brackets ka cross product kholna hai.
Plan: distributive law (Question 7 (iv)), \(\underline{x} \times \underline{x} = \underline{0}\) aur \(\underline{v} \times \underline{u} = -\underline{u} \times \underline{v}\) (Question 7 (ii)).
steps:
Diya gaya hai: koi bhi vectors \(\underline{u}, \underline{v}\).
Saabit karna hai: \((\underline{u} + \underline{v}) \times (\underline{u} - \underline{v}) = -2(\underline{u} \times \underline{v})\).
Tareeqa: Algebra mein \((x + y)(x - y)\) jaise kholte hain waise hi kholenge, lekin ek bari shart ke saath: har cross product mein tarteeb wohi rakhni hai. Phir Question 7 mein definition se saabit kiye hue qawaneen lagayenge.
Dilchasp baat: algebra mein \((x + y)(x - y) = x^2 - y^2\) hota hai, lekin yahan jawab bilkul alag aata hai, kyunke cross product commutative nahi.

Brackets kholein
\[(\underline{u} + \underline{v}) \times (\underline{u} - \underline{v})\]
\[= \underline{u} \times \underline{u} - \underline{u} \times \underline{v}\]
\[+\ \underline{v} \times \underline{u} - \underline{v} \times \underline{v}\]
Kyun: Distributive law dono brackets par. Pehle bracket ka har vector doosre bracket ke har vector se cross hua; minus sign scalar \((-1)\) hai jo cross product se bahar aa jata hai (Question 7 (iii)).

Simplify karein
\[= \underline{0} - \underline{u} \times \underline{v} - \underline{u} \times \underline{v} - \underline{0}\]
\[= -2(\underline{u} \times \underline{v})\]
Kyun: \(\underline{u} \times \underline{u} = \underline{0}\) aur \(\underline{v} \times \underline{v} = \underline{0}\), kyunke apne aap se angle 0 hai aur \(\sin 0 = 0\). Aur \(\underline{v} \times \underline{u} = -\underline{u} \times \underline{v}\). Is tarah do dafa \(-\underline{u} \times \underline{v}\) aaya, jama ho kar \(-2(\underline{u} \times \underline{v})\).
Dhyan dein: Agar \(\underline{v} \times \underline{u}\) ko \(\underline{u} \times \underline{v}\) samajh lein to beech ke terms cancel ho jayenge aur jawab ghalti se \(\underline{0}\) aa jayega.

Misaal se tasdeeq
\[\underline{u} = \underline{i},\ \underline{v} = \underline{j}\]
\[(\underline{i} + \underline{j}) \times (\underline{i} - \underline{j}) = -\underline{k} - \underline{k} = -2\underline{k}\]
\[-2(\underline{i} \times \underline{j}) = -2\underline{k}\]
Kyun: \(\underline{i} \times \underline{j} = \underline{k}\), \(\underline{j} \times \underline{i} = -\underline{k}\), aur \(\underline{i} \times \underline{i} = \underline{j} \times \underline{j} = \underline{0}\). Dono taraf \(-2\underline{k}\), to formula sahi hai.
